#511. Producer Kevin J. Walsh Had Seen It All. Then ‘Being Heumann’ Came Along

📅 13 Nov 2026

Producer Kevin J. Walsh Had Seen It All. Then ‘Being Heumann’ Came Along

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-features/being-heumann-kevin-j-walsh-1236754923/

Diungkapkan bahwa the oscar-nominated producer helped open doors for the disabled community on the set of sian heder's latest pic: "i'm as proud of what we did behind the scenes to redefine access as i am of the quality of this movie. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, being heumann producer kevin j. Walsh is not easily rattled.

Berdasarkan laporan, after all, the boston-area native served in a variety of assistant roles for scott rudin, steven spielberg and tommy mottola before eventually spending more than five years running ridley scott’s company, scott free. There, he shepherded a dozen pictures, four of them directed by Scott, including All the Money in the World (2017), The Last Duel (2021), House of Gucci (2021) and Napoleon (2023). In other words, he’s as battle-tested as they come.

Berdasarkan laporan, yet the prospect of helping coda director sian heder tell the story of judith “judy” heumann’s herculean fight to make the world more accessible for disabled people made walsh’s blood run cold. Related Stories Movies Sam Levy, Jamie Ramsay Offer Advice to Up-and-Coming Cinematographers: "What You Guys Do Lives Forever" Movies Ridley Scott Will Miss Academy's Governors Awards, Accept Honorary Oscar Remotely (Exclusive).

Sebagaimana diketahui, “when sian first asked me, ‘why do you want to do this?’ my answer truly was, “because the movie fucking terrifies me,’” walsh tells the hollywood reporter in support of being heumann’s nov. 13 release on Apple TV.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in 1977, disabled rights activist judy heumann helped organize the landmark section 504 sit-in, a nationwide protest aimed at compelling hew secretary joseph califano to finally sign the long-delayed regulations implementing section 504 of the rehabilitation act of 1973. Heumann and her fellow disabled activists occupied federal buildings across the country for more than three weeks until Califano finally put pen to paper.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the regulations secured civil rights protections for disabled individuals and helped direct billions of dollars toward making federally funded infrastructure more accessible, including through curb cuts, wheelchair ramps, wider public restrooms and designated parking spaces. The movement also helped pave the way for the more sweeping Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990.

Berdasarkan laporan, walsh and heder knew that if they were going to dramatize heumann’s david-versus-goliath tale, the only way to honor the late disabled pioneer was to bring her story to the screen authentically. That meant casting more than a dozen key roles with disabled actors and practicing what the movie preaches by creating an accessible, equitable set that could accommodate the ensemble’s unique needs.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the rub was that no such blueprint existed, and there was only one wheelchair-accessible trailer in all of north america. Working alongside a ten-person accessibility team and a crew that included disabled artisans and technicians, Walsh, Heder and their partners customized the Being Heumann set, taking extra precautions for the cast and ensuring direct access to personal and hair/makeup trailers.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “we did experience a handful of califano-type people, just not from the studio side. It was more, You can’t do it this way. It’s never been done this way,” Walsh shares. Apple was great. “But we needed to ignore history and really try to recreate how people make movies. I’m as proud of what we did behind the scenes to redefine access as I am of the quality of this movie. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, michael patrick thornton, who plays a supporting role opposite ruth madeley’s lead turn as judy, put matters into perspective in a way walsh will never forget. As one of the most accomplished disabled screen and stage actors of the last 25 years, Thornton found that Being Heumann offered him a first-time experience that most actors likely take for granted.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “on his first day, he got into the hair and makeup trailer and started to cry. He said, ‘In my whole career, I’ve never, ever seen the inside of a hair and makeup trailer,’” Walsh recalls. “He went on to describe it to me personally and said, ‘You don’t understand. But I feel like I’m one of everyone here. Normally, I’m in a closet getting ready on my own. This is Shangri-La for an actor who’s disabled. ’”.

Below, in a conversation with THR, the Manchester by the Sea producer also discusses his company’s prolific output in the 2020s, plus his extensive upcoming film and TV slate.

Berdasarkan laporan, when we last spoke for napoleon three years ago, the actors’ strike had just ended, and there were a lot of questions as to what the new normal would be. What did the answer end up being for you and The Walsh Company?.

Diungkapkan bahwa we’ve been lucky. Echo Valley did have to shut down because of the writers’ strike, so we went back to finish it. We got to make three or four movies during the strikes, which was really something. We were able to keep shooting in Europe. Overall, we’ve now made five movies at Apple since [launching the Walsh Company and signing there in 2022]. We then got a little independent film made called Miss You, Love You, and we’ve since made four films at Apple. So COVID and the strikes impacted us, but we were largely able to keep going.

Is it harder to set things up now? Or is it about the same?.

Diungkapkan bahwa it’s been about the same for us. The head of a streamer once joked, “Everybody’s been drinking at the bar for free, and now they’ve got to pay their tab. We’ve been on a really good pace setting things up, but getting things made and securing that green light is always harder. ” So those days are gone when a streamer would green-light a $50 million to $70 million movie and say, “Hey, good luck. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i have to really work for the green light now, but these streamers and studios need product. So I’m lucky to be in that small percentage of people who are still getting movies produced. We’ve set up a bunch of movies, and we’ve made five since we last talked. We’ve also started a TV business.

Diungkapkan bahwa you and sian heder both have deals at apple. Did they play matchmaker between the two of you for Being Heumann?.

Diungkapkan bahwa i actually met sian during a party at ben affleck’s house. I had been looking for the right thing, but Apple ultimately did play matchmaker because we both had deals there. We both grew up outside of Boston, and we both expressed a desire to work together. They said they needed someone to come on alongside [producer] David Permut, who had identified the rights and done a great job developing the script. So Sian and I really bonded as we started to talk about the challenges of this movie, and I was excited to jump in with her.

Sebagaimana diketahui, you mentioned your fellow producer david permut. Do you know the story of how he fended off Jean-Marc Vallée to acquire the rights to Judy Heumann’s story?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i don’t know the details surrounding the jean-marc of it all. I do know that David and Sian arrived at Judy separately, but then they quickly came together. I came in much later, but I was really happy to play a pivotal role in the development of the script and the execution of the movie.

Sebagaimana diketahui, judy was at a decision-making point when sian cold-emailed her [in 2020]. One of Sian’s best friends, who was an accessibility coordinator on Crip Camp, had told her to watch the documentary [co-starring Heumann]. m. ” Judy wrote back 20 minutes later and said, “I’m making the decision on who I’m going to make this movie with today. Sian asked, “Why should I watch it?” And her friend said, “This woman needs to have a movie made about her. So if you can get on the phone with me tonight at 5:00 p. , you’ll be in the running. ” So Sian watched Crip Camp, and she emailed Judy that same day to say, “Hey, I’m really interested in your story. ” Sian quickly finished her book and called her that night.

Sebagaimana diketahui, coda came out in august 2021. Sian’s follow-up is now out in November 2026. It won the Oscar for best picture in March 2022. Was she indecisive about how she wanted to spend her Oscar capital? Or did it just take a while to get Being Heumann across the finish line?.

Berdasarkan laporan, i think she’s just really exacting. She’s relentless in making sure something is really excellent, well done and well researched. So she took her time just to make sure it was the movie she wanted to commit to. People misuse the word picky when exacting is the better word. She had a lot of opportunities with other films and studios, but they weren’t quite the right fit for her or an exact match with her DNA.

Diungkapkan bahwa she really appreciates and supports underdogs — and this story certainly tells the ultimate underdog story. So it took time for her to get the script right, and then it took time for Apple to finally make that turn to say, “Okay, we’re going to make Being Heumann. ” That’s just part of the normal process of getting movies green-lit.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i’m ashamed to admit i never fully realized how life-changing a curb cut could be for someone with a disability. And, as the movie points out, so many people were naive to that reality. But after watching Being Heumann, I’ve started noticing all the other forms of accessible infrastructure that Judy Heumann and her allies fought to establish.

Diungkapkan bahwa you’re right that people don’t realize it. People do not realize how vital and how prevalent curbs cuts and other forms of barrier-free access are. Judy fought for them at a time when they didn’t exist. This affects everyone. One of my favorite lines in the movie is about how anyone at any time can become a part of this subset of disabled people. We’ve done probably 15 Q&As over the last month, and you’d be surprised how many people are affected, whether it’s personally or through their siblings, their parents, their cousins, et cetera. And if we’re lucky enough, we’ll live a long time — long enough to use a cane or a walker or a wheelchair.

Diungkapkan bahwa hollywood, meanwhile, still has very few figurative curb cuts for the disabled community, whether it’s telling their stories or hiring their performers. Did you encounter your own Joseph Califano types in trying to get this movie made?.

Diungkapkan bahwa we did experience a handful of califano-type people, just not from the studio side. It was more, You can’t do it this way. Apple was great. But we needed to ignore history in a way and really try to recreate how people make movies. It’s never been done this way. I’m as proud of what we did behind the scenes to redefine access as I am of the quality of this movie.

Diungkapkan bahwa access is the word i keep coming back to for everything about this movie. We made sure that disabled people had access to every single thing that an able-bodied crew member had access to — and then some. We created a film set with access to trailers and ramps. That happened through a lot of hard work, ingenuity and research by our great team of people.

Did any wheelchair accessible Star Waggons exist?.

Berdasarkan laporan, there was one in all of north america. We actually ended up cutting the backs off some trailers and creating lifts to bring actors up into the hair and makeup trailer. We had a series of ramps built by our construction team and grips, which we laid out to lead actors to any trailers that weren’t accessible. It made such a difference.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one of our actors, michael patrick thornton, who plays ed roberts, the self-described “artichoke” in the movie, had been working for 30 years in the movie business. He’s a huge Broadway actor and a big TV actor. He just finished a Broadway run with Keanu Reeves in [Waiting for Godot].

Sebagaimana diketahui, on his first day, he got into the hair and makeup trailer and started to cry. He went on to describe it to me personally and said, “You don’t understand. But I feel like I’m one of everyone here. This is Shangri-La for an actor who’s disabled. They asked him what was wrong, and he said, “In my whole career, I’ve never, ever seen the inside of a hair and makeup trailer. ” I was so floored by that story and what we had done to achieve it. Normally, I’m down the hall in a closet getting ready on my own. ” So, as a seasoned disabled actor, he could see the difference.

Was there extra crew to accommodate the disabled cast?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, we had a 10-person accessibility team at all times. We provided masseuses, nutritionists and round-the-clock care. We had people transferring disabled actors from their regular wheelchairs to period wheelchairs. We’d give them time for stretches and breaks. We had a lot of disabled crew members working with us as well.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but we made a lot of mistakes throughout the process. It’s one of the reasons why I did the movie. We had to refine it and hone it and get it better and better. ” I wanted to figure out all these issues. When Sian first asked me, “Why do you want to do this?” my answer truly was, “Because the movie fucking terrifies me. It was just really important for me to learn this new skillset. But with a good team around us, we were able to achieve it.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there are so many great disabled actors in this movie who had never acted before. So, for them, it was like, This is how movies must work all the time. They’d never been in a film before, much less a soundstage or a set. (Laughs. ).

When it came to casting Judy and the other 504 protestors, how large was the talent pool of disabled actors?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, you might be surprised to hear this, but there are a lot of really talented people. Our casting directors, Bernie Telsey and Adam Caldwell, really put the spotlight on that community. Had we not tried to authentically cast people with the actual disabilities of the characters they’re portraying, we wouldn’t have found that talent.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for judy, it was a bit more specific. We had to find a disabled person who has the charisma and acting chops to lead a movie, but also possess the same kind of ferociousness and tenacity that Judy had. So there aren’t a lot of Ruth Madeleys out there.

Hopefully, this movie opens more doors for everyone.

Berdasarkan laporan, yeah, my hope is that people will shine a spotlight on these actors so that they’ll be considered for other parts. We’re developing a TV show right now for an A-list TV actress, and I’ve pitched one of our disabled actors, Andrew Pilkington, to play her sibling. So I just said, “How great would it be if he were the brother of this actress? That would provide a whole other layer of complexity to this show. He plays Hale Zukas in Being Heumann, and he communicates with the antenna on the board. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa i’m also doing the team hoyt movie at netflix with producers gotham chopra and tom brady, and [directors] nat faxon and jim rash. I’m bringing Andrew Pilkington on because he’s a producer in his own right, and he’s going to help me with authenticity. We have an actor who has cerebral palsy, and he’ll oversee the way we make the movie.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, so there is a lot of talent in front of the camera and behind it. It’s just a matter of redefining the norms of casting actors in movies and TV shows and learning to look at everyone all at once. Again, access.

One of the best performances of the year was given by a disabled actor named Steve Way on the series Furious, which was partially directed by Cory Finley, who you helped launch by way of Thoroughbreds.

Diungkapkan bahwa yes, steve is incredible. I just read in the trades a couple days ago that Ramy Youssef and Steve are doing a body swap comedy, which is really interesting. She chatted with him, but Steve had some conflicts regarding this movie. What Steve and Cory and [creator] Liz Meriwether did on that show is amazing. We’re actually getting ready to start prep on Cory’s next film. Sian knows Steve. It’s coming up next year with a really good cast.

Berdasarkan laporan, i admire how honestly being heumann portrays its disabled characters. In other words, the film doesn’t portray them as infallible saints simply because they’re disabled. They’re generally altruistic, but they still make mistakes and give in to their impulses, like we all do. Did the ensemble also appreciate this unvarnished take?.

Diungkapkan bahwa they totally did. One of the most amazing feats of the movie is that each person you meet has their own little 180-degree turn. Early, early on, before prep, I said, “There’s too many people to service, Sian. I’m glad you mentioned that because one of the geniuses of Sian Heder is that she’s able to create an arc for all 15 of these characters. And I will say she proved me wrong. I don’t know if you’re going to get around to all of it. ” And she did. And so the actors loved that.

Diungkapkan bahwa a lot of times, when we see disabled characters, they’re either perceived as saintly or bitter because they’re dealing with their disability, but they are like anybody else. They just happen to be in a wheelchair or unable to access certain things that non-disabled people have access to. So the actors really appreciated how layered and different all these characters were.

Diungkapkan bahwa i was also impressed by how they let their personal experiences shine through in their characters quite a bit. If you recall the testimonials in the movie, Sian wisely guided and directed them to look inward a bit as they were telling those stories about their disabilities. That infused the film with a certain credibility, but also emotion.

Mark Ruffalo and Dylan O’Brien both fit their roles so well, but the cynical viewpoint is that you needed a couple names to appease the powers that be.

Berdasarkan laporan, they just responded well to the material. Stick to this number, but go make the film. [Apple TV bosses] Zack Van Amburg, Jamie Erlicht, and Matt Dentler really got behind this movie and said, “Go make the film. Don’t get me wrong, it’s always beneficial to have movie stars help open a film and bring awareness to a film. ” So we didn’t need any real names. But Apple was supporting this film through and through, head to toe. We were just lucky to get Mark and Dylan.

Berdasarkan laporan, mark is a once-in-a-generation-level actor. He could be perceived as a cold, simple villain, but he’s really a guy who’s just trying to do his best. He is perfect in the role of Califano. I spoke to him this morning in fact. We’re working together on another project that he’s going to star in and direct. It’s a very complex, layered part. And at the end of the day, he tips his hat to Judy, nicely, by saying, “Well fought. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa dylan is another wonderful actor with a huge following, so we got lucky to have those guys help raise awareness of the film. But we didn’t really need them.

Diungkapkan bahwa the postscript says that the fight for disability rights is far from over. Do you happen to know what the outstanding issues are?.

Berdasarkan laporan, yeah, a lot of these section 504 rights and regulations are now being conflated with the argument about transgender rights. They all fall under the same umbrella. So, in 14 states right now, they’re trying to repeal funding for some of these Section 504 rights because of other rights that fall under that umbrella. There was a big article about this in Time magazine within the last couple of months.

Sebagaimana diketahui, what people don’t understand is that you’re talking about taking away curb cuts, elevators and access for disabled people in our community. If you’re against the idea of a person in a wheelchair being able to access a federal building, a post office or a place to get their passport renewed, you’re on the wrong side of history. This is why it’s super important, and it saddens me that we’re still having this conversation 50 years later. It’s just that simple. So you have to look closely at what you’re reading, what you’re voting for and who you’re supporting.

Diungkapkan bahwa i spoke to tom pelphrey and louis leterrier not too long ago, and your sci-fi action-thriller with them, liminal, came up. What else are you excited about on the Walsh Company slate?.

Berdasarkan laporan, i’m really excited about louis’ movie. Besides Tom, it has Vanessa Kirby, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II, Tracy Letts and Franka Potente. He’s got a murderer’s row of great actors. So we’re in post on that right now.

Diungkapkan bahwa we’ve also had a rocket-ship start to our tv business. We hired an executive named Danny Feldheim about a year and a half ago, and we’ve set up ten TV shows in that time. We have five or six shows at Apple, a show with John Mulaney and Langston Kerman at HBO and another great show called The Hawk with Dave Collard and Casey Affleck at Hulu. So we’re excited about being all over that side of the business.

Sebagaimana diketahui, we’re also prepping three or four movies for next year. We just got something in the last week that I’m most excited about. There’s a Black List script called Best Seller that was with Peter Rice until he left to take the [Netflix CCO] job. We got lucky enough to meet on it, and while it went out to 10 or 15 producers, we won that movie. So we’re really excited about putting it together and getting a director on it.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, we’re finally going to make adam and aaron nee’s next movie, calamity hustle, next year. We’re getting close on that deal with two actors.

Ryan Reynolds and Channing Tatum are no longer attached?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it’s no longer ryan and channing. The Nee brothers have done a really good job on the script, and they’re ready to go. It’s going to be a couple other actors, but we’re really excited about it. They’ve said no to a lot of movies to make this movie.

You mentioned it earlier, but what’s the latest on Cory Finley’s next one?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, yeah, we’re going to make cory’s upcoming film [reasonable people] with paul rudd and sam rockwell, which will probably be a fall shoot. It’s a wonderful story about revenge in modern-day America. We’re out to another actor now, and we’re closing a deal with a really exciting financier who’s going to do it. It’s kind of like a present-day Hatfields & McCoys set in the suburbs. It has that same darkly comedic tone as Thoroughbreds, with really nuanced characters and a deep dive into the relationship between two fathers and one of the fathers’ brothers in this suburban community.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, then we have a really big film at apple that we’re getting quite close on for next year. It’s a Christmas movie. So it could be a busy year next year, but I’m honestly just lucky and happy to be making movies and doing what I love. Apple has been great to us, and I’m grateful they’ve given us a platform.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “obsession and backrooms” has been the most repeated phrase this year. Everyone’s been trying to discern what the takeaway should be. Rather than simply hiring more YouTubers or adapting unusual internet properties, is the real lesson to take chances on newer, original voices, regardless of platform or genre?.

Berdasarkan laporan, you’re right about original voices. Matisse Haddad, who wrote Best Seller, is an original voice. He has a Black List script called Drudge about Matt Drudge, which is also one of the best scripts I’ve ever read. There’s another great young writer named Cody Brotter who’s writing the Bon Jovi story for us at Universal. It’s one of her early screenplays, and it’s one of the best scripts I’ve read in a long time. We’re going to try to get that made.

Diungkapkan bahwa so it’s about finding young voices and just trusting youthful filmmakers. There’s a great script we love called The Toe by a writer named Mallory Westfall. It’s harder to make those kinds of movies. It’s completely bonkers and left of center and dark, but original and great and unlike anything you’ll read. Those [tonal seesaws], like Cory’s next movie, are harder lifts, but you’re fighting for originality at the end of the day.

Sebagaimana diketahui, there are filmmakers to be found on youtube, just like there’s filmmakers to be found everywhere. The directive at our company isn’t, Go find us an action movie or a romantic comedy. It’s just about keeping an open mind to originality and setting your own pace and not trying to copy something else. It’s always, What makes you sit up straight when you read it? Do you want to make it and why? That’s really all we look for.

Berdasarkan laporan, we’ve reached the dreaded ai question. But now there’s filmmakers like Doug Liman and Darren Aronofsky who are experimenting with it rather aggressively, while directors like Ben Affleck, Danny Boyle, and Ava DuVernay have acknowledged using it for minor details, such as animating old photographs. Initially, the creative community drew a hard line in the sand against its use. But as the scope keeps creeping outward, those minor details could soon become major ones, and entire departments could be gutted or downsized in no time. Maybe I’m being an alarmist, but do you think it’s inevitable at this rate?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i don’t think you’re being alarmist, but i don’t think it’s inevitable, either. There’s always going to be human artistry that you need to harness.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, some people say, “graphic designers and previs artists and other visual artists are going to be gone. He did Boston Strangler with me. ” John P. Goldsmith, who was my production designer on Being Heumann, has a degree from Harvard — a master’s in architecture. On Being Heumann, he designed all the detailed lobby work, like the brass elevator buttons and the marbling, in the building the protestors storm. John took all of his education, his history, his experience, all of it, and made sure that it looks right. He’s a genius. All of that was constructed from scratch. People from Apple came to visit the set, and they couldn’t believe it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it hearkens back to one of my first films in my early 20s when i worked as an assistant on the hours. So, Stephen Daldry, I believe, described the [dropped] shot to the production designer and the construction team. I walked through it, and I couldn’t believe how exact a match it was. We didn’t want to go back to the hotel location. It was flawless. The next morning, I came back to the stage at Pinewood, and the hallway of this hotel had been reconstructed. We dropped a shot while filming at a hotel in the south of London, and we moved back to the stage. We put the actors in the hallway, Julianne Moore, and we had the shot.

Sebagaimana diketahui, so, yes, there’s a way to use ai quite a bit in previs, in post and with vfx, but you still need to harness that type of human creativity. You need to have a team that executes at a high level. This is a community medium. You’re going to use AI as a tool. The filmmakers you mentioned — Danny, Ava and Ben — they’re using it as a tool in a great way. But if you ask any one of them, “Can you do away with human artistry and do your job?” they’d say that you can’t. I could not make Being Heumann without my producing team of Sian, David, Kevin Cleary and John Beach.

Berdasarkan laporan, we are using ai, for sure, with certain vfx stuff. There’s definitely some AI in the previs on bigger movies. But I came up working in a lot of different departments in moviemaking, and you will always need to harness artistic creativity. Without it, you’re going to have a movie that feels devoid of spirit. It’s going to look mechanical, and audiences are going to sniff it out.

Sebagaimana diketahui, starting with “the invite,” this might be your finest hour as an actor. On paper, it sounds like a movie Seth Rogen would make. Playing Joe, did you feel you were doing something you hadn’t done before? Did you have one of those out-of-body experiences?.

Diungkapkan bahwa as we were making the movie, i felt like i was being given the opportunity, at least in a movie, to do something that was very representative of my exact comedic, tonal and dramatic taste. What was really amazing about what Olivia did was that she allowed us to affect the tone of the film with our performances. She allowed me to insert humor in moments where it wasn’t originally going to be, which changes the tone of the whole thing. And then she allowed me to make jokes that subverted those moments in ways that weren’t originally scripted.

Berdasarkan laporan, to me, that was an incredibly new and gratifying feeling. You could see it happening in real time. We weren’t just being invited to change the dialogue or our characters throughout the performing process. You could see that a scene was much funnier than we thought it would be. Or we thought a scene was going to be funny, but it was actually much more intense than we all thought. Olivia was allowing us to change the tone of the film itself with our performances. We were encouraged to play with that and not be too beholden to what it was originally conceived as, but instead feel it out as we were doing it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i have to give her credit for using my stuff in a way that turned out very well. Berdasarkan laporan, people like julia louis-dreyfus, bryan cranston, samira wiley and abbi jacobson, along with so many of the amazing cast members, were honestly really helpful in getting the movie made. Berdasarkan laporan, “darkwing duck” because i’m a child of the ’80s and ’90s. Congratulations on the Emmy for “The Muppet Show,” and obviously we have “The Studio” Season 2 coming. Sebagaimana diketahui, are there other disney shows from the ’80s and ’90s you’d love to bring back? i think of “talespin,” “gummi bears” and “ducktales. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i always think of “flight of the navigator. If we can get “Gargoyles” back up and running ….

Sebagaimana diketahui, that would be great. I did love “Gargoyles. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, let’s talk about “the studio” season 2. There have been a lot of reports from the set: Madonna, the Venice Film Festival. Which real-life awards-season humiliation of yours is going to end up on the show?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, we have several of those. We wanted to get people we were even bigger fans of and make them even bigger parts of the episodes, if we could. Some are really unbelievable, and having to direct these people has been among the most terrifying moments of my entire life. For ourselves, we really tried to be even more ambitious. We also wanted to dig deeper into our own feelings about the industry and our own internal conflicts as we go about all this.

Does the awards race feel more or less relevant to you now? Having made “The Studio,” how does it look compared with 15 years ago?.

Diungkapkan bahwa what’s interesting is that until i did the “steve jobs” movie, which was pretty deep into my career, i was never part of anything that was on that journey in any capacity. But that was the first time I went to Telluride, and then we were in the New York Film Festival. I’d been to TIFF and South by Southwest to premiere things. So it’s interesting, because I had a very lovely career before any of this was even on my radar.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but that being said, the fact that “the studio” won awards got us things in the second season that we probably wouldn’t have gotten in the first season. So there is some tangible outcome to some of this stuff. And I’ve seen people go on the journey and not get the outcome they wanted, and they had a good time and seemed to have good perspective at the end of all of it. I’ve seen people go on this journey and get the exact outcome they were hoping for, and it ultimately gave them none of the things they hoped it would. I understand why people get invested in it, and I understand the lure and the draw. It is a fascinating part of our industry to me.

Berdasarkan laporan, i think especially for smaller things, it is incredibly helpful. But what’s interesting is those people are at these events right next to the people whose lives it will change. If you’ve already made many billion-dollar movies, winning best picture is a feather in your cap. It could make or break people’s careers. It could make or break a film. It could change the course of people’s lives. For some people, they’re at the point of their career where awards have very personal stakes, but there are many other people here for whom the awards have real-life stakes. It’s not going to change the course of your life, per se. To me, that is really interesting to see in real life and really cool. Will they get to do the thing they’ve always wanted to do, or will it not happen the way they hoped?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, that is really interesting and scary and cool to see play out. There are those moments where your heart is pounding and you’re like, we’re doing it. This is what we asked for: to put ourselves out there and subject ourselves to reality in terms of how our work is being perceived. It can be very gratifying and incredibly scary and stressful.

Can you tell me something about “The Studio” Season 2? Is there a oner episode again?.

Diungkapkan bahwa we actually try to do much more of that. There are more episodes in a much more condensed timeline. They’re real-time, half-hour moments in time that the episode is chronicling.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it’s a weird time in the industry. Depending on who you ask, the future looks very grim. Others say it’s an evolution and we’re just going through some changes. One of the biggest conversations here at Middleburg was Peter Rice going to Netflix. Someone like him, who’s been such a theatrical guy, making that move feels like a signal: Theatrical’s back! How do you feel about this moment? Do you get nervous, or do you think we’re going to be OK?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it’s a mixture of everything. The fact that so many people are going to theaters, compared to the last few years, is so encouraging. It reminds me of when I was a kid, honestly, a little bit more. As someone who loves going to the movies, it’s really fun to see. I think we are finally getting over that hump of the pandemic and the strikes and all that. It is everything at once. It seems like things are returning to a time when there are a lot of good movies and people are willing to go see them, and that’s really exciting. From my own personal lens, I can go to the theater on a Tuesday night and it’s packed and it wasn’t like that for a long time. I’m very optimistic about some things. And I think other things are terrifying.

Berdasarkan laporan, “sethical. ” Friends from growing up still call me that when I see them. They don’t even think about it. It just comes out.

Something you loved as a kid but can’t believe you were into when you think about it now?.

If karaoke went away altogether, I’d never need to be in a room with some drunk person screaming a song ever again. That said, “All for Love” by Bryan Adams. I hate it. The rooms are getting smaller and smaller. It used to be the bar was higher because you were subjecting yourself to a real big room full of people. Now I’m three feet away from this person. It’s so loud. If you have two other raspy-voiced friends, it’s a really good song.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i was going to say “the apartment. ” I would take “The Apartment. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i’m pretty flexible. I can almost get my leg behind my head.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i just like vanilla. I did that movie with Barbra Streisand [”The Guilt Trip”], and she was obsessed with McConnell’s ice cream, which is from Santa Barbara. Every scene we shot, she’s like, “Wouldn’t we be eating ice cream in this scene?” So yes, it’s become McConnell’s.

Sebagaimana diketahui, my glasses come to mind. My shoes. Things like that.

What TV show or film in all of history do you wish you were a cast member of?.

Maybe it would have been cool to be in “Ghostbusters” or something like that.

Which fictional character do you most relate to or admire?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i always liked homer simpson. Not that I relate to or admire him, but I always just liked him.

Your favorite piece of advice, either given or received?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i was told at a very young age to write what only i could write, which meant writing things based on my own experience, things that were happening to me. Don’t talk about fucking crazy glue. Talk about that. I was writing jokes that were observational, like, “What’s the deal with crazy glue?” Those kinds of jokes. No one else can talk about that. I was maybe 15, maybe 14 and he pulled me aside and said, “Dude, you’re out there trying to get hand jobs and trying to buy beer and trying to sneak into parties and shit. I was doing OK. ” It was honestly the best creative advice I’ve ever gotten. Any asshole can write that joke. A stand-up comedian named Darryl Lenox, who’s passed away, unfortunately, told me that and he was really nice to me. I try to adhere to it to this day.

Sebagaimana diketahui, at the heart of this story is a villainous company called the brownstone corporation. The fictional company is deeply involved in artificial intelligence and is led by foreign investors based in the Middle East. Blackstone is said to have invested significant amounts of money in new artificial intelligence data centers and are intent on ensuring their long-term success.

Berdasarkan laporan, fitz defeats brownstone with a meticulous plan, and one that begins long before the grand finale. Berdasarkan laporan, fitz uses this cloak, along with his many other weapons, as he infiltrates a brownstone party, held to celebrate their recent successes and the launch of their plans. Berdasarkan laporan, his actions culminate in a one-on-one showdown with the leader of a group of bosnian mercenaries contracted by brownstone. Initially, his choice comes across as a mistake, as the mercenary gets the upper hand and seemingly has Fitz on the ropes. Despite displaying ruthless tactics against his other opponents, Fitz makes the interesting decision to fight the villain honorably, rather than shooting him dead right away. But unbeknownst to him, Fitz had attached two parts of an explosive device on his back and chest, allowing him to blow an explosive hole in the man's torso.

It was a finishing move that had somewhat of a sci-fi edge to it, but still felt consistent with the technologically advanced arsenal of weapons Fitz had at his disposal throughout the movie.

Sebagaimana diketahui, fitz also had a small helping hand from the recently fired sheriff of the community, olivia thirlby's parker. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in the closing minutes of the movie, fitz travels to the middle east, where he targets the company’s founder and leader. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it was the methods of the aforementioned villain who made all of this necessary. Berdasarkan laporan, as is the case with every ai data center, a significant amount of water is needed in order to keep them going. Brownstone recognizes this and, as such, is actively working to build cooling centers that would help keep the technology at a healthy temperature. For this, the company needs a sizable amount of land, and they had identified the town of Valentine in the countryside of Wyoming as a prime place for their cooling centers.

Diungkapkan bahwa in its efforts to make sense of the lengths they were willing to go to get what they wanted, ghost soldier addressed the matter of imminent domain, a law that enables property to be seized if it serves the good of the community. As characters in the story pointed out, the villains would have had to wait longer than they preferred for imminent domain to kick in, and expectations placed on them to get results spurred them to take matters into their own hands.

Sebagaimana diketahui, brownstone is no more, but fitz still has more to do. Fitz has thus far been lying low in his lab at Wyoming, even when he knows the government could use him elsewhere. The United States has all sorts of problems to concern itself with, from Russia to China, which were both brought up in their conversation. That setup could create room for a sequel if the new Jim Caviezel-led action film performs well at the box office.

Diungkapkan bahwa winter says officials have found no evidence linking the two incidents, pushing back on speculation that microsoft's technical issues may have played a role in the aviation disruption. The FAA has not publicly confirmed or denied whether the two incidents are related.

The clarification comes amid a chaotic day for travelers, with the FAA's nationwide shutdown raising concerns about flight operations across the country.

Diungkapkan bahwa transportation secretary sean duffy said faa technicians were investigating the communications failure. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin also said there was no evidence of a cyberattack or other national security threat, describing the incident as a telecommunications outage.

Berdasarkan laporan, meanwhile, microsoft has been dealing with its own massive outage, which began thursday and affected millions of users worldwide. Outlook, Teams, Copilot, SharePoint and other Microsoft 365 services experienced disruptions, impacting businesses, government agencies and other organizations.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, microsoft has attributed its problems to a technical issue involving a network capacity upgrade and subsequent network changes, saying it found no evidence of malicious or cyber activity. The company had begun restoring services Friday, although some users continued experiencing issues.

Despite the overlap, Winter's reporting suggests the two major outages are separate incidents, with officials not finding evidence that Microsoft's technical problems contributed to the FAA's nationwide shutdown.

The FAA's investigation into the communications failure remains ongoing.

Berdasarkan laporan, the first episode debuts on the jordan tv youtube channel sunday, with new episodes dropping each week. Warner Bros. worked with Jordan Brand on the docuseries.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “space jam really was more than a movie, it was a cultural movement and really changed the face of the entertainment industry, with an athlete like michael coming in,” says jordan brand cmo caitlin sargent, in an interview with the hollywood reporter. “The last thing you would have expected of an athlete like that would be going and filming a movie. So it was quite unconventional, and I think we always take that as inspiration. He’s our blueprint to say how can we do things a little bit differently?”.

Diungkapkan bahwa “what we decided was to leverage this moment and the story of space jam 30 years, really inspiring the next generation to find their own greatness,” sargent added. “We wanted to use that as a moment to reposition this channel with the six-part mini doc, and the goal here was no doubt to to make sure that we were telling the untold stories of the making of Space Jam, but also the cultural impact it had. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, but it is jordan tv that may be the more intriguing part of the launch. Jordan Brand, the Nike-owned athletics brand known for its iconic “Jumpman” logo, is rethinking content, betting that high-quality original programming, delivered directly to consumers via YouTube, is the future of how it engages with that audience.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i think we know how important storytelling is with the next generation, and we know how important youtube and that channel is,” sargent says. “And so we are working on repositioning our Jordan YouTube channel to Jordan TV, which is really what we’re calling inside access. It’s a one-stop shop destination for never been seen storytelling around product stories and experiences, really allowing our community and our consumer to come inside the walls of the Jordan brand.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “this is our first step out to really reposition the channel, and what you’re going to see is an intersection of sport culture and sneaker culture,” she adds. “But the main piece is that we want to make sure that it does feel like it’s that inside access. I always say, when we’re doing our storytelling, our branded content is always really amazing. But what really our young consumer wants to see is the making of, what was it like to be on set as we’re shooting? What was it like bringing that brand experience to life? And so this will really feel like you’re getting that through several stories that we’ve got coming and that we’re really excited about. ”.

As The Hollywood Reporter reported in an August cover story, brands are becoming more ambitious in their storytelling, looking beyond traditional commercials and campaigns to become more full-funnel storytellers, funding original content, and bringing consumers inside their worlds.

Sebagaimana diketahui, that’s true for nike, which was featured in the story, but also for jordan brand. Sargent describes the move as being an imperative.

Berdasarkan laporan, “we know our consumer has changed, and what creates an emotional connection with youth today is different than what it what it has been over the last 40 years,” she says. “So what we’re doing right now is trying to make sure that we’re shifting into, less branded content. If it feels like an ad, smells like an ad, it starts to fall a bit flat. What we really want to do is shift into a space where we’re creating core memories with our young consumer through the products, through the stories, and through the experiences that we’re putting forth. ”.

#525. HBO’s 5-Part Crime Drama Has One of the Best Seasons in TV History

📅 14 Nov 2026

HBO’s 5-Part Crime Drama Has One of the Best Seasons in TV History

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.polygon.com/the-wire-season-4-recommendation/

The Wire’s fourth season provided a far deeper look at Baltimore’s problems.

The Wire’s fourth season provided a far deeper look at Baltimore’s problems.

Diungkapkan bahwa at the turn of the 21st century, hbo was the place for prestige crime drama. The launch of The Sopranos in 1999 paved the way for the 2002 premiere of The Wire, which focused on drug dealers in Baltimore and the police officers trying to disrupt their operations. The series is still one of the best shows of all time, and provided breakout roles for huge stars like Idris Elba and Michael B. Jordan. But while it was compelling from the beginning, The Wire truly achieved perfection in season 4 when the scope expanded beyond the drug trade to examine the cycle of institutional failure.

Sebagaimana diketahui, season 1 of the wire was tightly focused on the drug empire of avon barksdale (wood harris) and his business-savvy second-in-command stringer bell (elba). Season 2 shifted the focus to the city’s port system, a jarring change as many characters faded into the background to make room for the tragic tale of the Sobotka family. The show could find comedy in something as simple as cops struggling to get new furniture into their office, and then gut audiences with the death of a relatable drug dealer. Showrunner David Simon quickly established a brilliant mix of humor and pathos. Season 3 was the most tightly linked to the show’s first season, largely completing the story of the Barksdale gang.

Berdasarkan laporan, that made season 4 perfect for a soft reboot, a shift that was defined by star dominic west all but disappearing after his relentless detective, jimmy mcnulty, was demoted for pissing off his bosses too many times. criminals beats are familiar, they become just one part of a far more ambitious season that fully capitalized on Simon’s knowledge of the city. (Simon worked as a journalist at The Baltimore Sun for 12 years before creating The Wire. Lester Freamon (Clarke Peters) effectively steps into the McNulty role of pursuing the truth, even when his supervisors would love for him to be a little less dogged, bringing a new methodical nature to the investigations instead of McNulty’s brash confidence. But while the cops vs. The detectives he previously worked with in the major crimes unit continue their work, investigating a vicious new gang that’s filling the void Barksdale left behind. ).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the season’s largest secondary plot involves the students at a baltimore middle school where former cop roland pryzbylewski (jim true-frost) begins teaching. By the end of season 4, the system has profoundly failed almost all of these kids, driving them to lives of addiction and violence. You want to root for all of them, from the ambitious Randy Wagstaff (Maestro Harrell) to the fiercely protective Michael Lee (Tristan Wilds). The young actors do a phenomenal job establishing likable characters in terrible circumstances. The Wire was always good at making most of its characters sympathetic, but seeing children trapped in such a brutal cycle really drives home the show’s themes of how crime thrives when institutions fail.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that theme also plays out in the mayoral campaign of tommy carcetti (aidan gillen). Gillen’s oily performance as a political survivor who would doom his city to satisfy his own ambitions was what landed him the role of Littlefinger in Game of Thrones. Carcetti was introduced in season 3 as an ambitious city council member, but he really shines in season 4 as he runs on reforming the Baltimore Police Department — and then quickly breaks his promises. Carcetti is even more compelling a character because he feels like a man who could have done good if he’d been willing to make sacrifices rather than feed his own ego.

Diungkapkan bahwa the wire season 4 is able to build so many new arcs because of the strong foundation established in the previous three seasons. The show is dense with rich characters who have grown significantly over the years even as they continue to struggle with many of the same problems. The cops and drug dealers alike feel world-weary as they deal with a more violent new generation represented by Marlo Stanfield (Jamie Hector) and his vicious enforcers Snoop (Felicia Pearson) and Chris Partlow (Gbenga Akinnagbe). Combined with the dark fate of most of the kids and Carcetti’s broken promises, the season creates the bleak feeling that everyone is trapped in a cycle of misery and decay.

Sebagaimana diketahui, season 5 gave most of the wire’s characters satisfying ends to their arcs and delivered a scathing critique of the downfall of american newspapers, commentary that has only become more profound 20 years later. But overall, it’s a big step down from season 4, spending too much time on a goofy fake serial killer plot and not enough on the nuanced character-driven stories that made season 4 feel so authentic. There are no bad seasons of The Wire, but season 4 perfectly achieved the show’s goals. It’s an alternately funny, tragic, and profound look at the complex ways that people are betrayed by systems that never really give them a chance to succeed.

We held off on season 4 until I was sure I could survive. Although there was an article in the Times a week before the COVID shutdown that explicated how vital the NYC DOE was as a social safety net, and that made me feel both great and depressed.

#530. ‘The Rings of Power’s Best Storyline Kicks Off With an Emotional Death

📅 14 Nov 2026

‘The Rings of Power’s Best Storyline Kicks Off With an Emotional Death

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://collider.com/the-rings-of-power-season-3-earien-death-numenor-storyline/

Editor's note: The below contains spoilers for The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 Episode 2.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it's likely that the rings of power plotline that longtime fans of j. R. R. Tolkien's larger Middle-earth saga are most invested in is everything regarding Númenor. Certainly one of the draws of exploring the Second Age is seeing this island kingdom at its peak, as well as the inevitable descent into civil unrest between two warring factions vying for the nation's well-being. But only two episodes into its third season, the Prime Video series raises the stakes when Eärien (Ema Horvath), the daughter of Elendil (Lloyd Owen), is discovered as a spy for the Faithful, leading to a harrowing self-sacrifice that no one saw coming.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, eärien's mere existence in the rings of power was an issue for some viewers. Having officially joined the Faithful in the five years between the second season and the third, Eärien works stealthily under Ar-Pharazôn (Trystan Gravelle), feeding intel to her father through her brother Isildur, who has returned home. After all, Elendil is said to have two sons — Isildur (Maxim Baldry) and Anárion (Andrew Richardson), with the latter finally arriving this season — but not a daughter. Created specifically for Prime Video's adaptation, Eärien has always been presented as a woman torn between loyalty and duty, and Season 3 has finally forced her to pick a side, despite the high cost. Upon being discovered, however, she chooses not to betray her family or convictions, but rather to throw herself from Pharazôn's window, a drastic but understandable action that costs her life. Although Rings of Power had finally pushed Eärien to the right side, her sudden demise reminds us that the threat the Faithful are facing is real — and that Númenor is worse off than things may appear on the surface.

From new projects in beloved franchises to festive holiday films.

Berdasarkan laporan, there's an argument to be made that the rings of power has always been at its best when it's given the númenor plot the time of day. From what's revealed up front, it feels as if The Rings of Power aimed to spend the season exploring Isildur and Eärien's strategic rebellion, but all of that quickly changed when Eärien was discovered and thus flung herself onto the streets of Armenelos. Elendil was one of the more interesting and complex characters in the first season, and Tar-Míriel (Cynthia Addai-Robinson) is, naturally, essential to the nation's fate. From the moment viewers return to the island kingdom, the show sets up a game of undercover cat and mouse, as Eärien attempts to balance complex political maneuvers with keeping a low profile. While last season began the conflict between the King's Men faction and the Faithful, Season 3 gives the struggle real legs. Although Eärien refuses to betray her kin or the Faithful, her betrayal has forced Pharazôn's hand, as he aims to wage war against his fellow Númenóreans.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as elendil and míriel wrestle for power against pharazôn, the rings of power seems to be setting up the cataclysm to come. This is exactly what occurs in the vision that Míriel has in the first season after contact with the palantír, and it's undoubtedly where the Prime Video series is heading. This angers Eru Ilúvatar, the God of Tolkien’s world, who not only annihilates Pharazôn and his forces, but, like the biblical Great Flood or the tragedy of Atlantis, sends a massive wave to destroy Númenor itself. In Tolkien's writings, he reveals that Pharazôn eventually forces Míriel to marry him before Sauron (Charlie Vickers) seduces the ruler into a full-scale assault on Valinor to usurp the Valar in an effort to claim eternal life for Men. That said, even with the outcome in mind, how Númenor gets there has always been the most interesting part of that story — with Eärien's demise being one more step toward that ultimate fate.

Berdasarkan laporan, of course, elendil and his sons have a destiny of their own, one that doesn't include their fallen daughter and sister. Elendil would abandon the depraved Númenor to establish the united Kingdoms of Gondor and Arnor, kingdoms his sons would inherit. Not only does Aragorn reunite the fractured kingdoms, but he becomes pivotal in the final defeat of Sauron centuries later. Through this royal lineage, Aragorn is eventually born during the Third Age. Now, it's hard to say when exactly this will all take place in The Rings of Power, but we can rest easy knowing the show has not only firmly set its course, but is now driving full-speed ahead.

New episodes of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power are available for streaming Wednesdays on Prime Video.

(Milo Ventimiglia), and how they shift and ebb and flow over the years. I LOVE Rocky IV, but it doesn’t have the emotional depth of I, II, or VI, and let’s not even talk about Rocky V.

Those remasters are part of a larger plan to reinvest in Fallout games — including Fallout 5, which is currently in pre-production — and a new untitled project at Obsidian Entertainment.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "we have multiple fallout projects in active development right now," bethesda said in an official announcement this summer. That includes Fallout 5, which is described as the studio's "long-range destination," and "a major Fallout 76 expansion" planned for 2027 called Raven Rock, which will serve as a prequel story to Fallout 3.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, bethesda also confirmed two long-standing rumors, announcing remasters for fallout 3 and fallout: new vegas. The studio did not provide any further details or a release window, but the projects have reportedly been in the works for many years. The existence of a Fallout 3 remaster dates back to at least 2020, when the project's existence was revealed through court documents related to the Federal Trade Commission's (FTC) litigation regarding Microsoft's buyout of Activision Blizzard.

Diungkapkan bahwa fallout 3 and fallout: new vegas' remasters follow last year's release of the elder scrolls 4: oblivion remastered, which was co-developed by virtuos and bethesda game studios. Bethesda also marked the 10-year anniversary of Fallout 4 in 2025, with the release of Fallout 4: Anniversary Edition. That rerelease included the original game, all six of the previously released DLC add-ons, as well as over 150 items pulled from the Fallout 4 Creation Club.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, fallout 3 was originally released in 2008 for playstation 3, windows pc, and xbox 360. C. The game was the third major installment in the Fallout series, and the first to be developed by Bethesda after acquiring the rights to the franchise from Interplay Entertainment. Fallout 3 is set in and around Washington D. 200 years after a devastating nuclear war, and players control a 19-year-old Vault dweller in search of their missing father.

Diungkapkan bahwa fallout: new vegas followed in 2010, and was developed by obsidian entertainment. It was set in the Mojave Desert and casts players as a courier who becomes embroiled in a conflict between various factions who are vying for control of the region.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in addition to new fallout games, a third season of the fallout tv series is in the works and recently wrapped filming. Bethesda Game Studios is also hard at work on the next game in its fantasy role-playing game series: The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel is now in development.

Despite its dark narrative, Revenge of the Sith features some of the most impressive and memorable sci-fi visuals in the entire Star Wars franchise.

Berdasarkan laporan, time travel has inspired plenty of complicated science-fiction stories over the years, though one of the most entertaining and arguably most accessible is back to the future, directed by robert zemeckis. Transported from 1985 to 1955 in a time-traveling DeLorean, Michael J. Fox's Marty McFly is endlessly entertaining as he attempts to make it back to his own timeline with help from Christopher Lloyd's Doc Brown before his own existence is erased. Across the board, Back to the Future is one of the most perfect sci-fi blockbusters, including its sequels, proving that not every sci-fi has to be so dark and serious.

To this day, Christopher Nolan's Inception has one of the most fascinating sci-fi premises, exploring the idea of infiltrating one's dreams using the classic tropes and concepts of a heist film with professional operatives stealing information from the subconscious, and the unique challenge of planting an idea in a target's head without them realizing it wasn't their own.

Sebagaimana diketahui, starring leonardo dicaprio, joseph gordon levitt, elliot page, tom hardy, and more hollywood legends, inception is easily one of the greatest and most original sci-fi films on this list, one that trusts viewers to keep up with its admittedly complicated ideas for the sake of providing some brilliant visuals as it showcases the "architecture of dreams. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, denis villeneuve's arrival takes the alien invasion premise and turns it on its head, putting the themes of communication and connection at the forefront rather than the typical narratives of violence and humanity being on the brink of extinction. Rather than treating the visiting aliens as straightforward threats, language and its effects on a species serve as the central sci-fi concept, with a linguist played by Amy Adams gradually having her perceptions of time shifted the more she learns their language.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the result is one of the most beautiful and captivating sci-fi films in the modern era. While Arrival might not have the usual fast-paced stakes or conflict seen in other sci-fi epics, Villeneuve still managed to create solid tension all the same.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, thanks to interstellar, christopher nolan absolutely deserves to be on this list twice. An incredibly bold space epic with a mission to save humanity as a dying Earth becomes harder and harder to inhabit, the true dangers of space are on full display with one of the most scientifically accurate sci-fi movies of all time.

Diungkapkan bahwa interstellar is also one of the most emotionally devastating on this list, particularly as matthew mcconaughey's cooper is forced to leave his children behind. Just like in Inception and subsequent films on this list, composer Hans Zimmer further cements himself with Interstellar as a key architect of how sci-fi movies sound in the modern era. The film may have some clunkier dialogue and exposition in some places, though that certainly doesn't keep it from being one of the best sci-fi movies of all time, especially with its massive scale of space and time being contrasted with a strong thematic focus on family throughout.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the terminator is easily one of the most influential science-fiction action movies ever made, introducing audiences to a terrifyingly classic dystopian future where humanity has nearly been wiped out by its own robotic creations. Also featuring time travel, James Cameron's iconic film details the robots' effort to end the war before it can even begin by sending a Terminator back in time to kill the mother of humanity's greatest leader/savior in the future.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the sci-fi premise is brilliantly simple, making for one of the best sci-fi action movies of the 80s, and arnold schwarzenegger's performance made the terminator a huge cinematic icon. Despite its more modest scale, the impressive use of physical effects helped make the world and its mythology incredibly fascinating, and it's no wonder that the movie has generated as many sequel projects as it has.

Diungkapkan bahwa showcasing the dangers of unchecked scientific power in one of the most fantastic ways possible, steven spielberg's jurassic park brought dinosaurs back to life in a way never experienced before. A personal favorite of mine, the blending of groundbreaking visual effects and practical animatronics ensures that the early 90s movie still holds up quite well today. While the movie naturally generated multiple sequels and an entire Jurassic franchise, none have managed to fully rival the original.

Sebagaimana diketahui, james cameron's aliens is perhaps even more impactful on the sci-fi genre than the terminator, the sequel to ridley scott's original film that elevated the original concepts into a major horror-action film. Expanding the Alien universe with new technology, characters, and brand-new ways to make Xenomorphs even more dangerous, Cameron's Aliens is one of the best examples of a sequel finding its own unique identity while still building on the foundation of what made the first entry so captivating in the first place.

Berdasarkan laporan, when we're talking about some of the best sci-fi movies since the original blade runner, it only makes sense to include its epic follow-up with denis villeneuve's blade runner 2049. Another solid example of a sci-fi sequel finding its own unique identity while honoring the original material, 2049 takes place decades after the original, following replicant Blade Runner K (Ryan Gosling) as he uncovers a discovery that could massively change the relationship between humans and artificial life.

Diungkapkan bahwa naturally, k's investigation eventually leads to harrison ford's rick deckard, providing a strong connection to the original film while gosling's performance knocks it out of the park. The cinematography is also on another level, expanding the world and future of the first movie rather than just repeating it.

The Matrix may very well be one of the most perfect sci-fi movies of all time, particularly the first chapter directed by the Wachowskis.

After learning the truth about his life and digital existence, Neo (Keanu Reeves) chooses to wake up to the much harsher reality as "The One" who's capable of changing the dark future humanity has found itself in.

Sebagaimana diketahui, featuring groundbreaking visual effects, reeves remains one of the biggest sci-fi action icons thanks to the matrix for good reason. Featuring several philosophical ideas about reality and free will, the movie goes beyond typical blockbuster spectacle as well, making it one of the most enduring and best sci-fi achievements of all time, much like Blade Runner.

#540. Bloodborne Just Got A Complete Overhaul On PC

📅 14 Nov 2026

Bloodborne Just Got A Complete Overhaul On PC

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://screenrant.com/bloodborne-pc-overhaul-path-tracing-mod/

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, bloodborne's status as a playstation 4 exclusive has caused no shortage of complaints over the years, especially now that over a decade has passed without any platform update. While it's perfectly functional on the platform, the frame rate could be a lot better, and those without a PS4 have long hoped for it to be more widely available.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in the meantime, fans have been making it a lot more accessible on pc. Fans seeking to play it on their computer can choose between either an emulated solution that's received plenty of updates over time or a more recent native decompilation port (which unfortunately made some use of AI in development). If you want to double down on the latter, a new lighting overhaul takes things even further.

Berdasarkan laporan, bloodborne pc path tracing, uploaded to nexus mods by ssoullxx, delivers a full suite of ray-traced features to the unofficial pc port of bloodborne. The description lists its additions as follows: "ray traced moonlight, global illumination, shadows, reflections, puddle mirrors and glass, with DLSS Ray Reconstruction. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the project is currently an alpha build, meaning that not everything will look correct in the new version as it stands. That being said, those who have already played Bloodborne countless times could still appreciate a new look for the game, and future updates might deliver more thoroughly on the potential for a ray-traced version. It's also possible to toggle the overhaul on and off while playing simply by pressing F9, so there's no real commitment involved here.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it's certainly been cool to see the community work on bloodborne over the years, but as with many fan projects, recent months have seen a major turn toward ai-assisted coding. On top of the AI assistance involved in the unofficial Bloodborne PC port, the Nexus Mods page for the Path Tracing mod features a disclosure noting that "AI produced the majority of the code, or the UI, or the voice, the dialogue, the translations, music, or other assets. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, opinions on ai coding vary greatly, but there are at least a couple of reasons to think twice before gleefully installing vibe-coded ports or mods. To begin with, AI code is typically going to be less efficient than that of a skilled human programmer, increasing the odds of poor performance or problems that might not be present in 100% human work. The environmental impact of running large language models is also worth considering, especially in light of the sheer volume of projects using AI to generate code.

Sebagaimana diketahui, when it comes to lighting, there's also the simple matter of bespoke design. The original version of Bloodborne features atmospheric lighting from the hands of FromSoft's skilled designers, which even a human-coded ray-tracing mod would run the risk of losing. There's no denying that this mod is a drastic overhaul of Bloodborne, but whether the iconic game is in need of one is a question that anyone considering an installation will have to decide for themselves.

Berdasarkan laporan, “the victim stood in the driveway between the car she arrived in and the car tiffin hadn’t returned,” police said in the press release. An altercation occurred, and Tiffin shifted the car into reverse and hit the gas pedal, hitting his brother with the open door and pinning his mother between the two cars. “Tiffin and his boyfriend were in the car, and the brother opened the car door to confront them. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, after she was hit, curthoys was taken to a hospital. She died from her injuries on October 12.

Detectives conducted a nearly monthlong investigation before an arrest warrant was issued on Tuesday, November 10, for Tiffin’s arrest.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, authorities reported to the home where curthoys was hit, and “officers began searching the house, warning tiffin the k-9 would bite him if he didn’t come out. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, “after getting no answer, the k-9 located tiffin in a bedroom. Sebagaimana diketahui, it’s not currently clear whether tiffin has entered a plea or retained legal counsel following his arrest. The investigation into the case remains ongoing.

We will vigorously defend this action and are confident that the courts will vindicate Michael Mann’s statutory rights under the Copyright Act.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the director's stance is that the script for heat was his own original work, as it was an adaptation of his novel of the same name. Berdasarkan laporan, despite the timing of the lawsuit, mann's representatives assured viewers that the legal battle won't affect the production of heat 2. Diungkapkan bahwa heat 2 serves as both a prequel and a sequel to heat, following lapd detective vincent hanna and master thief chris shiherlis before and after the events of the original film. William and Melanie were ultimately declared cancer-free in late 2024.

In April, William was forced to deny a cruel hoax claiming that he’d been diagnosed with stage IV brain cancer.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “[facebook groups] have created stories that say i have stage 4 brain cancer, was in some kind of fight with erika kirk and that i’m dying,” he explained via x. Most of the stories use an AI image of me. “All their stories are monetized. Facebook Support will not remove the page. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa he clarified that “none of these stories are true,” adding, “they apparently seem genuine enough for fans to repost them across social media and send messages of support to me and my family all while the culprits behind the account make money. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “this is the downside of ai and yellow journalism,” he argued. “While [AI] can be a wonderful tool in the right hands; it can be used as a weapon in the wrong hands. If you see a bizarre story about me; unless you see it posted on one of my verified accounts take it with a grain of salt. ”.

#547. Lindsay Arnold Breaks Down Sister Rylee Arnold's ‘DWTS’ Fitness Routine

📅 13 Nov 2026

Lindsay Arnold Breaks Down Sister Rylee Arnold's ‘DWTS’ Fitness Routine

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.usmagazine.com/celebrity-body/news/lindsay-arnold-details-sister-rylees-dwts-fitness-routine/

Lindsay Arnold is revealing how younger sister Rylee Arnoldis staying in tip-top shape ahead of the Dancing With the Stars season 35 semifinals.

“My baby sister’s snatched physique is going viral right now, well deserved, and I’m here to give you all the secrets,” Lindsay, 32, a former DWTS pro herself, began a Thursday, November 12, TikTok video.

Lindsay noted that as a certified personal trainer, she designed Rylee’s fitness routine to better focus on “more consistent workouts” more than one year ago.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the movement club fitness app founder explained that rylee, 21, asked her to create a program for her so that she could maintain her stamina off-season and feel like “she never stepped away” from the ballroom. (Rylee and season 35 dance partner Connor Wood are about to enter week 10 of the competition and are inching closer to the season finale. ).

Rylee also asked about “increasing her muscle tone and muscle definition,” which Lindsay took into account while tailoring her program.

Berdasarkan laporan, “as an oldest sister, when a baby sister comes to you and wants help or wants your advice on something, it’s the best day ever,” lindsay gushed. “So I immediately got her onto a full workout regimen, as well as incorporating some supplements into her everyday routine. ”.

Before season 35 of DWTS began, Lindsay said that her sibling did six days of workouts with one rest day.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i would always start her with 30 minutes of cardio,” the mother of three explained, noting that the types of cardio would vary between a stationary bike, treadmill at a 12 incline and three speed, followed by a “30 to 45 minute movement club session. ”.

Rylee also followed her sister’s six-week Advanced Weights program, which uses five to 20-pound dumbbells, a workout bench and resistance bands.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “rylee followed along with [it] religiously, which was so cool to see,” lindsay shared. “I’ve been so proud of Rylee and her consistency in moving her body and working towards her goals and obviously it’s been a huge payoff. ”.

Once Rylee began her DWTS journey, Lindsay said they “shifted” her fitness regime since she was already dancing up to nine hours a day.

Sebagaimana diketahui, lindsay explained that instead of focusing on the advanced weights program, she pointed rylee to her app’s pilates x strength program. It combines the “incredible lengthening and flexibility” of Pilates-style workouts with “strength and weighted” workouts.

Berdasarkan laporan, “then cardio every day is based on her preference and energy levels,” lindsay shared, pointing out that “the dancing and rehearsals that she’s doing is providing an incredible amount of cardio into her routine. ”.

Lindsay, who exited DWTS in 2022, admitted that being a pro on the show gives dancers an amount of cardio that “isn’t realistic in everyday life” and is definitely a factor in Rylee’s toned physique.

As the season has progressed, Lindsay told Rylee to “focus on protein intake,” and encouraged her to add 5 mg of creatine into her daily routine to support her muscles and keep building strength.

Berdasarkan laporan, “speaking from experience of being in that position [on dwts], i always found that during a season, with the amount of cardio demands on you and the amount of calories that you are burning through in a day with a rigorous schedule,” lindsay explained. “I found it was really hard for me to maintain my muscle definition and tone throughout a season. ”.

Lindsay ended her video by showing Rylee some love and applauding her hard work on and off the dance floor.

Diungkapkan bahwa “rylee is absolutely incredible. What she’s able to manage and do in her days, she’s amazing,” she said. “I’m so proud of her across the board: her work ethic, her talent, her choreography ability has just been absolutely off the charts this season, and I could not be more proud of her. ”.
